listenings.text: I have listened to something like three thousand senior introductions, and almost all of the weak ones make the same two mistakes. The first is listing tasks. People tell me everything they do in a week, and by the fourth item I have lost the shape of the job. A list is not a scope. The second is starting with an apology, and it is nearly always about English. Nobody in the room was going to think about your accent until you pointed at it. And here is something people find hard to hear. The size of your team is the least interesting number you can give me. Forty people, four hundred people, it tells me almost nothing. What decisions do you make that nobody above you reviews? That is the real question. So I ask everyone the same thing now. In one sentence: what breaks if you leave tomorrow? If you can answer that, you can introduce yourself anywhere.

Twelve years ago I turned down a job I still think about. It was a bigger title at head office, a team of two hundred, and a much shorter commute. I took a smaller role instead, running one market, with real accountability for the number. My mother thought I had lost my mind. If I had taken the head office job, I would have had a wonderful title and almost no decisions. And I would not have learned the thing that actually made my career, which is how to lose money, and how to explain losing it to a board without losing the room. Nobody teaches that. You only learn it when the number is yours. One piece of advice about telling this story. Tell it as judgement, not as luck. Say what you chose and why you chose it. If you tell it as something that happened to you, people hear a passenger. If you tell it as a decision, they hear a director.

extra_audio.text: I spearhead commercial operations across Latin America for an Italian insurance group. I oversee a cross-functional team of forty and I liaise with Milan above the local limits. Below those limits, the accountability for the region is mine. If I had stayed on the technical side, I would never have built the broker network.

paras: The Group is pleased to announce the appointment of a new Commercial Director for Latin America, effective this quarter. The role spearheads commercial operations across four markets and oversees a cross-functional team of forty, spanning commercial, claims and underwriting support.

The scope of the position covers Brazil, Colombia, Mexico and Argentina. Anything above the local authority limits is handled in liaison with the group head office in Milan; below those limits, accountability for the regional result sits with the Director. The role reports directly to the Global Head of Commercial.

The appointment follows a year in which the regional corporate portfolio drove the majority of growth. The Group leveraged the broker network built over the previous three years; if that network had not been in place, the corporate result would have been broadly flat.

The immediate priorities are alignment across the four markets on a single set of quarterly deliverables, and a review of climate exposure in the south. The Director will work with regional counterparts and with stakeholders across the broker network. Group HR will publish the full leadership profile next month.
